A1.justification: Both PDFs describe EBCAR. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and support reliable matching of retained, relocated and added content.

before.justification: v1 reports original ConTEB ranking and throughput measurements, component ablations, MS-MARCO v2 evaluations and candidate-size experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds E5-based evaluations, a query-embedding training comparison and qualitative attention analysis.

M1.justification: The structural encodings, hybrid attention, fixed-query InfoNCE objective and inference procedure remain unchanged. Section 3.2 elaborates the already-local document-ID assignment. The updated-query variant is introduced as an ablation, without replacing the proposed method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same three ConTEB training datasets, eight ConTEB evaluation datasets and MS-MARCO v2 evaluation with TREC 2021/2022 queries. The new E5 experiment reuses existing ConTEB tasks and changes the retrieval configuration.

E2.justification: Section 4.6 adds E5 alone as a directly evaluated retrieval baseline against EBCAR using E5. Comparator membership in the retained ConTEB tables, TREC comparison and candidate-size experiment is unchanged.

E3.justification: Added experiments introduce an E5 retrieval/embedding configuration, a fixed-versus-updated query control, and attention inspection using 20 randomly sampled test queries per dataset with final-layer weights averaged across heads. Previously stated splits, budgets, metrics and default model settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 substantially expands diagnostic evidence with a query-embedding stability ablation in Appendix A.1, retriever robustness testing in Section 4.6, and sampled attention analysis in Appendix A.5. These test additional questions about optimization, retriever dependence and information flow beyond the retained component and candidate-size ablations.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. Figure 3's across-dataset distribution summaries are unchanged. Sampling queries and averaging attention heads in the new analysis do not introduce run-level uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: v2 adds E5-only and E5-with-EBCAR scores across eight datasets, including 62.78 versus 77.36 on MLDR and 6.05 versus 80.64 on Football. Training-loss curves and attention patterns add substantial findings about optimization and information flow. All numerical entries in Tables 1–4 remain unchanged; the E5 scores concern a new configuration.

T1.justification: The reranking formulation, attention-mask definition and InfoNCE objective in Equations 1–2 are retained. Added document-ID examples and mechanism explanations introduce no new mathematical result, assumption or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions and conclusion retain the same central claims about embedding-based efficiency, structural hybrid attention and context-aware ranking performance. The additional experiments support these existing contributions.

C2.justification: v2 adds dataset-specific interpretations of component ablations, interprets E5 results as evidence of retriever independence, and explains the new attention and training-stability observations. It also explicitly discusses incorporating new documents without retraining. Existing embedding-bottleneck, multi-positive and candidate-size limitations remain.

D1.justification: The future code-release promise becomes a reported public EBCAR repository in the abstract and reproducibility statement. v2 also supplies a ConTEB access link and clarifies local document-ID reindexing and frozen-table reuse. Existing hyperparameters, hardware and baseline implementation details are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds Wang et al. (2024b) for E5. The related-work positioning remains unchanged; the Qu and Warner citation updates refer to retained works and represent publication-metadata changes.

P1.justification: Localized expansions explain document-ID assignment and attention through examples. v2 adds Section 4.6 and appendix subsections, relocates the LLM-usage statement, and updates the publication header, affiliation and bibliography. The main narrative and section sequence are otherwise retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds a training-loss figure, two attention heatmaps and boxed examples, and expands Figure 2's caption. Figures 1–3 retain their artwork; the candidate-size plot moves from Figure 4 to Figure 5. Existing tables retain their structure, with placement and sizing adjustments.

improvement.justification: v2 provides direct evidence for query stability and robustness beyond Contriever, clarifies document-ID handling, and supplies reported code access instead of a release promise. These improve support and reproducibility while preserving the original results. The gains are bounded: attention evidence is qualitative, and one added retriever does not fully establish the broad retriever-agnostic interpretation.
